1	# drop
     2	
     3	A public "send me files" page. Anyone can drag files onto it; nobody but the
     4	owner can get them back out.
     5	
     6	- Drag-and-drop upload ([Uppy](https://uppy.io)) over [tus](https://tus.io): 50 MB
     7	  chunks, automatic retries, resume after a dropped connection or a reloaded tab.
     8	- The uploader gets nothing back: no list, no links, no delete.
     9	- When a send finishes, the owner gets an email with a link to a private page for
    10	  that send: download each file or all of them as a .zip, then delete them from the
    11	  server.
    12	- The link is the only credential (a random 192-bit token). There is no login.
    13	- The owner can also make **share links**: download-only, no delete, no sender
    14	  details, expiring after 1, 7 or 30 days, revocable from the owner page.
    15	
    16	## Screenshots
    17	
    18	The data below is made up: names, links and addresses are examples.
    19	
    20	**The upload page**, as anyone sees it, with three files queued:
    21	
    22	![Upload page with three files queued](docs/screenshots/upload.png)
    23	
    24	**Home mode, after an upload:** one box with the result and a share link ready to
    25	copy or send.
    26	
    27	![Finished upload in home mode with a share link](docs/screenshots/home-share.png)
    28	
    29	**What the recipient gets:** the files and nothing else.
    30	
    31	![Share page with two files to download](docs/screenshots/share.png)
    32	
    33	**The owner page:** downloads, share links with their state, and delete.
    34	
    35	![Owner page with files, a share link and the delete box](docs/screenshots/owner.png)
    36	
    37	**The admin page** (home mode only): disk use, 90-day statistics, inbox, outbox
    38	and history.
    39	
    40	![Admin page with disk meter, statistics, inbox, outbox and history](docs/screenshots/admin.png)
    41	
    42	## Home mode
    43	
    44	A visitor coming from the server's own public address is taken to be the owner at
    45	home (or on a VPN that exits there). For them the banner reads `HOME MODE`, and when
    46	an upload finishes the page offers a share link right away, with Copy and the
    47	system share sheet, so sending something to someone needs no email round trip.
    48	Home-mode uploads send no email; the finish screen links to their owner page
    49	instead. Their files are deleted once their share links run out (links revoked by
    50	hand don't count; with all of them revoked, the files stay), or a day after upload
    51	if no link was ever made.
    52	
    53	Expiry needs no extra machinery: a share link is checked against its expiry on
    54	every request, so it stops working on the second. The files go on the app's own
    55	5-minute cleanup pass, the same one that sends late emails and removes abandoned
    56	partial uploads.
    57	
    58	The server learns its public address by asking `HOME_LOOKUP_URL` (default
    59	`https://1.1.1.1/cdn-cgi/trace`, which answers with an `ip=` line) and compares it
    60	with Cloudflare's `CF-Connecting-IP`. There is no background polling: a matching
    61	visitor costs nothing, and a mismatch triggers a fresh lookup at most once per
    62	`HOME_RECHECK_SECONDS` (60), so a changed home address is picked up on its own.
    63	A failed lookup keeps the last known address; with none known, nobody is home.
    64	Set `HOME_LOOKUP_URL=` (empty) to turn home mode off.
    65	
    66	Home mode also links to `/admin`: disk use against the quota, 90-day statistics
    67	(sends received and downloaded, sends shared and fetched by their recipients, links
    68	made and used), uploads in flight, the inbox (sends to you, with their owner pages),
    69	the outbox (your shares, their links and whether they were fetched), and the
    70	history of deleted sends with why they went. Anyone behind the home address can
    71	open it; from anywhere else `/admin` is a plain 404.
    72	
    73	## Guards
    74	
    75	Because the page is open to anyone, the app protects the disk it writes to:
    76	
    77	| Setting | Default | Meaning |
    78	|---|---|---|
    79	| `MAX_FILE_SIZE` | `50G` | Largest single file |
    80	| `MAX_TOTAL` | `500G` | Everything stored, including uploads in progress |
    81	| `MIN_FREE` | `300G` | Refuse any upload that would leave less than this free on the volume |
    82	
    83	Space is reserved at the moment an upload is *created*, from its declared length,
    84	so several concurrent uploads cannot jointly overrun the limits. When an upload is
    85	refused for space, the owner is emailed (at most twice a day).
    86	
    87	`DATA_DIR` must contain a `.drop-volume` marker file. If the volume is not mounted,
    88	the marker is missing, so the app refuses uploads and `/healthz` returns 503,
    89	rather than filling the disk underneath the mount point. `REQUIRE_MARKER=0` turns
    90	the check off.
    91	
    92	Also: 30 new sends and 500 new files per hour per client IP (`CF-Connecting-IP`,
    93	or the first `X-Forwarded-For` address when that header is missing), at most 200
